newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC president says weak oil price hurting.
newsitem.headline: OPEC president says weak oil price hurting.

text.p: OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri said on Thursday that weak oil prices were again threatening OPEC member country economies.
"The hard fact is that this general mood of optimism faded away...with the risk of bringing OPEC member countries revenues and economies once again to a dangerously low level," he said.
The president was opening OPEC's summer ministerial conference and was referring to a 30 percent fall in oil prices since January.
"Clearly the present condition of the market is an unfavourable one," he said.
He said encouraging for OPEC was the recovery in Western economies and buoyant economic growth being registered in the Asian-Pacific region, especially China.
Al-Badri renewed OPEC's commitment to restraining oil supplies to ensure oil market stability.
"If the market is to develop in an orderly equitable fashion in the future, it is essential that we maintain our commitment," he said.
He said OPEC was monitoring developments on measures to combat global warming which he said might adversely affect future oil demand.
OPEC ministers agreed on Wednesday to freeze its output ceiling of 25.033 million barrels per day for the next six months.
